title: ISO 27001 Workflow Automation: What You Can Automate
summary: ISO 27001 workflow automation uses software to run your ISMS tasks and collect evidence automatically.
body_markdown:
## Where automation fails ISO 27001 audits


When a record has no named owner and can't be traced to a defined process, **automation fails the audit** , and those are exactly the records an auditor samples.


**40% of the more than 1,700 certified companies** in[DNV's analysis](https://www.dnv.com/article/insights-from-auditing-information-security-management-systems-162216/) had severe findings at their initial audit, against 60% that passed cleanly, meaning that obtaining security certification does not eliminate the risk of critical security flaws.


Two in five teams therefore reach certification with something structurally wrong. The four patterns below are how a workflow adds to that share.


Run an access review nobody documented through a workflow and you repeat an undefined step faster. The auditor asks for the procedure first, and the automation isn't the procedure.


### Evidence nobody reviews


Under clause 7.5.2, documented information must be identified and described, for example with a title, date and author. An export with no owner or timestamp fails on its face.


Alerts routed to a channel nobody triages are worse: the log proves the signal arrived and that nobody acted on it.


Pull the ticket, the configuration export or the log entry from the source system. A screenshot can't be re-queried, so the auditor has no way to confirm it's complete.


> Alerts routed to a channel nobody triages are worse: the log proves the signal arrived and that nobody acted on it.


Green means only that the checks you configured passed. It says nothing about whether the risk assessment is current, the internal audit (clause 9.2) happened, or management review (clause 9.3) took place.


Certification is a certification body's decision after it audits those things, so a dashboard can support your evidence but can't replace it.


Someone has to defend risk acceptance, exception approval and scope changes to an auditor. A workflow that auto-approves an exception leaves a timestamped record with no one behind it.
